- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- When sentiment is negative or mixed (≤0.5), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent price is trending down.
- Overshoots after strong upward moves (e.g., >75% from prior peak) are common; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 1–3% if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out extremes by averaging last 3–5 days’ price + sentiment signal.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2% lagged sentiment weight to forecast to align with sentiment momentum.
